title: The Breath That Took a Journey
intro: This quiz follows one breath of air as it travels through the respiratory system and helps the body receive oxygen.

questions.prompt: Where does air usually enter the body?
questions.explanation: Air usually enters the body through the nose or mouth.

questions.prompt: What tube carries air from the throat toward the lungs?
questions.explanation: The trachea carries air from the throat toward the lungs.

questions.prompt: What happens in the tiny air sacs called alveoli?
choices: Oxygen moves into the blood, and carbon dioxide moves out
questions.explanation: In the alveoli, oxygen moves into the blood and carbon dioxide moves out.

questions.prompt: What does the diaphragm do when you breathe in?
choices: It moves downward and gives the lungs more room to expand
It pumps blood into the lungs
It pushes air out of the nose
questions.explanation: When you breathe in, the diaphragm moves downward and gives the lungs more room to expand.

questions.prompt: Why do we breathe out carbon dioxide?
choices: The body makes it as a waste gas and needs to remove it
The body uses it to strengthen bones
It helps the stomach digest food
It turns into oxygen inside the nose
questions.explanation: We breathe out carbon dioxide because the body makes it as a waste gas and needs to remove it.
